# KiteConfig 2.0.0

The DSL reshape. You still write each value once. Where you write it, and who
applies it, both changed.

Old names do not compile, so nothing changes behaviour quietly. The upgrade
table is at the bottom.

## A complete setup is four lines

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.yuroyami.kiteconfig") version "2.0.0"
}

kiteConfig {
    appName = "Jetzy"
    appId   = "com.example.jetzy"
    version = "1.4.0"
    autoApply = true
}
```

`autoApply = true` is the one switch. With it on, an ordinary build applies
everything KiteConfig needs to change, including the files you commit. With it
off, nothing touches them until you run `./gradlew kiteApply`.

## What changed

**One switch instead of four permission blocks.** Every `rewrite { }` block is
gone, along with the `auto` flag inside each one and the task names that went
with them. `kiteApply` applies every selected platform. `kiteApplyAndroid` and
`kiteApplyIos` apply one, so an Android build can never drag iOS source edits
along with it.

**Platform differences live in the platform's own block.**

```kotlin
kiteConfig {
    appName = "Jetzy"
    appId   = "com.example.jetzy"
    android { appId { suffix = ".android" } }
    ios     { appName = "Jetzy Lite" }
}
```

Nothing is copied when a block opens, so a shared value written after a platform
block still loses to it. Declaration order decides nothing.

**A feature is on when you gave it what it needs.** Set `logo { foreground }`
and the icons are installed. A feature that needs nothing from you, like the
launch screen, asks for `enabled = true`. An empty `splash { }` no longer turns
anything on.

**Build numbers are text.** Android reads the one whole number Google Play
wants; Apple compares by numeric component, so a dotted build number finally
works there. `VersionSchemes.DEFAULT` produces exactly the digits it always did,
so an app already on a store keeps its numbering.

**Your Android manifest needs no KiteConfig lines.** The app label and the
splash theme used to require two hand-written attributes:

```xml
<application android:label="${appName}" android:theme="${kiteSplashTheme}">
```

KiteConfig now writes its own small manifest and lets AGP merge it over yours,
so a fresh Android project needs no edit. The old lines still resolve if you
keep them, and `kiteDoctor` points out a manifest value of your own that the
merge replaces.

**Blocks stay in their own scope.** `android { skip(ios) }` used to call the
root's skip and exclude iOS everywhere. It no longer compiles, and neither does
`ios { jvm { } }`.

## Fixed

- The Android splash resources reach an AGP 9 build. They went through the old
  source-set API, which AGP 9 refuses for generated output, so any project with
  the splash on failed to configure.
- A quoted brace or semicolon in the Xcode project is a value, not syntax. An
  app named `}` wrote a file the next run refused to parse.
- The iOS splash installs through the ownership machinery, so a hand-made PNG is
  recovered rather than silently replaced, a removed dark image is cleaned up,
  and nothing is committed before the art has been rendered.
- Each logo installer asks about its own platform. Excluding one used to leave
  both running.
- The bytecode level reaches Java as well as Kotlin, so a module with both
  languages compiles instead of failing on inconsistent JVM targets.
- `kiteCheck` refuses what an ordinary build refuses. It used to skip the model
  validation entirely.
- Each identifier is checked against the store that has the rule.
- A dark-only splash color is referenced by the night resources.
- `ignoreVersionGuards` reaches every adapter, including the KMP-native Android
  one that ignored it.
- Generated features activate from content, so configuring the extension object
  directly works the same as calling the block.
- The compatibility check is serializable, so the command CONTRIBUTING documents
  can be run as documented.

## Upgrading

| 1.0.0 | 2.0.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `id = "x"` | `appId = "x"` |
| `id("x") { android { suffix = ".a" } }` | `android { appId { suffix = ".a" } }` |
| `appName("x") { ios("y") }` | `ios { appName = "y" }` |
| `version("x") { formula { } }` | `version { scheme { } }` |
| `version("x") { android { reupload = 1 } }` | `android { version { rebuild = 1 } }` |
| `android { pin = 123 }` | `android { version { buildNumber = "123" } }` |
| `android { shipped = 1001003090 }` | `android { version { publishedBuildNumber = "1001003090" } }` |
| `ios { marketingVersion = "1.4" }` | `ios { version = "1.4" }` |
| `locales { pin("en") }` | `locales { tags = listOf("en") }` |
| `locales { filterAndroidRes = true }` | `android { locales { filterResources = true } }` |
| `logo { background = file(...) }` | `logo { background = image(file(...)) }` |
| `android:label="${appName}"` in your manifest | nothing: delete the line |
| `android:theme="${kiteSplashTheme}"` in your manifest | nothing: delete the line |
| `logo { backgroundColor = "#..." }` | `logo { background = color("#...") }` |
| `logo { android { safeZone = 0.6 } }` | `android { logo { foregroundScale = 0.6 } }` |
| `logo { desktop { roundMac = true } }` | `desktop { logo { roundMac = true } }` |
| `splash { }` turned it on | `splash { enabled = true }` |
| `splash { android { theme = "T" } }` | `android { splash { theme = "T" } }` |
| `jvmTarget = 21` | `jvm { target = 21 }` |
| `<topic> { skip(ios) }` | `ios { <topic> { enabled = false } }` |
| every `rewrite { }` block | `autoApply = true`, or run `kiteApply` |
| `logo { rewrite { replaceOld = true } }` | nothing: adoption is automatic and backed up |
| `ios { rewrite { targets("iosApp") } }` | `ios { xcodeTargets("iosApp") }` |
| `ios { rewrite { cleanPlist = true } }` | nothing: plist keys follow the facts |
| `ios { rewrite { onConflict = ... } }` | nothing: managed keys carry your value |
| `ios { rewrite { proMotion = true } }` | `ios { infoPlist { proMotion = true } }` |
| `ios { infoPlist = file(...) }` | `ios { infoPlist { path = file(...) } }` |
| `ios { rewrite { renameSharedModule(a, b) } }` | `ios { renameSharedModule(a, b) }` |
| `./gradlew kiteRewriteLogo`, `kiteRewriteXcode` | `./gradlew kiteApply` |
| `kiteConfig.id` | `kiteConfig.appId` |

Three things change meaning, not just spelling:

- A project with `logo { }` and no `rewrite { }` used to get desktop icons only.
  With `autoApply = true` it now installs the Android and iOS icons too.
- An empty `splash { }` no longer turns the launch screen on.
- `VersionCodeScheme.compute` returns `String`. A scheme returning an integer
  needs `.toString()`.

`only()` with no arguments used to mean "everywhere". It is now an error.

## Compatibility

Gradle 8.5 and newer, AGP 8.5.2 through 9.3.x, KGP 2.4.x, Compose 1.11 through
1.12.x, on a JDK 17 or 21 daemon.
